source.author: verg
source.text: Sic fatus, meritos aris mactavit honores, taurum Neptuno, taurum tibi, pulcher Apollo nigram Hiemi pecudem, Zephyris felicibus albam.
source.text_original: Sic fatus, meritos aris mactavit honores, / taurum Neptuno, taurum tibi, pulcher Apollo / nigram Hiemi pecudem, Zephyris felicibus albam.
source.text_english: Thus he spoke, and duly slaughtered sacrificial offerings at the altars: a bull to Neptune, a bull to you, beautiful Apollo, a black ewe to Winter, a white one to the auspicious West Winds.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Solent enim plerique gentilium daemones colere, ne noceant, et alios exorare ut praestent benecia: Unde et illud Virgilianum est: Nigram hyemi pecudem, zephyris felicibus albam.
reuse.text_original: Solent enim plerique gentilium daemones colere, ne noceant, et alios exorare ut praestent benecia: Unde et illud Virgilianum est: Nigram hyemi pecudem, zephyris felicibus albam.
reuse.text_english: For most of the pagans are accustomed to worship demons, so that they may do no harm, and to implore others to grant benefits. Hence also that line of Virgil: A black sheep for winter, a white one for the favorable Zephyrs.
